guideSights.name: Hotel Majestic
guideSights.note: Passeig de Gràcia 68. Enjoy city views from the rooftop. Just enter the elevator right from the lobby, and head up to the top floor.

guideSights.name: Park Güell
guideSights.note: A large urban park heavily influenced by Antonio Gaudi. The area was originally meant to be a residential property development with Gaudi doing much of the planning and landscape design. Only two houses were built and the land was later sol

guideSights.name: Park Güell, the main entrance
guideSights.note: Two Gaudi-style pavilions mark the entrance to the park and lead to the steps up to the Hipostila Room. In the middle of the steps is the dragon (or salamander) fountain that has become almost as much a symbol of Barcelona as the Sagrada Fa

guideSights.name: Hipostila Room and Grand Plaza
guideSights.note: At the top of the stairs from the main entrance is the Hipostila Room with its 86 white columns supporting the plaza above. The ceiling has a number of colourful mosaics. Above the Hipostila Room is the main terrace, which was meant to be t

guideSights.name: Gaudi House Museum
guideSights.note: Distinctive pink house that Gaudi lived in for nearly 20 years (although not designed by him). It features furniture designed by Gaudi and other objects relating to Gaudi's life. The gift shop has a large selection of Gaudi-themed souvenirs

guideSights.name: Turo de les tres creus
guideSights.note: This is the highest point of the park and where Gaudi wanted to build a chapel. After the development failed, Gaudi built a monolith with three crosses like Calvary instead. Be sure to take in the panoramic views of Barcelona.

guideSights.name: National Art Museum of Catalonia
guideSights.note: Has the single best collection of Romanesque art in the world, and a fine Gothic collection as well. Includes the ''Pantocrator'' from the Taüll Romanesque church. The building itself is also very beautiful.

guideSights.name: Archaeology Museum of Catalonia
guideSights.note: Situated on the Montjuic, it exhibits archaeological findings from Catalunia from different periods. Under 16 and 65+ free. €3 for others. Special discounts for other groups.

guideSights.name: Catalan Ethnographical Museum
guideSights.note: This museum mainly exhibits exponents, which were imported by Catalan sailors as they explored the new world. Free on the first Sunday each month (11:00 to 15:00)

guideSights.name: Olympic and Sports Museum Joan Antoni Samaranch
guideSights.note: The museum displays high-performance sport competitions, recreational sports, sports in general and sports for disabled people. It shows how sport can promote values, educate, innovate and renew. The museum has a sport idols space with outs
guideSights.en: Joan Antoni Samaranch Olympic and Sport Museum

guideSights.name: Botanical Garden
guideSights.note: Although a botanic garden had been established in Barcelona as early as 1888, the current gardens date from 1999.

guideSights.name: Miramar gardens
guideSights.note: This is where you arrive by a harbour cable car. Marvelous place in the spring, full of roses and fountains. Entrance to the cactus garden is nearby. The Mirador Miramar offers splendid views over the city.
